svg.title: GenerativeAI-powered chatbot solution
svg.desc: Retrieval-augmented chatbot on AWS - web frontend, authenticated API, RAG Lambda with an LLM provider, and a daily ingestion pipeline.

g.text: Chatbot solution to provide the sales department of the company with a virtual assistant, which can summarize knowledge base data and help quickly find relevant information.

text.tspan: Daily data ingestion. EventBridge Scheduler triggers an ECS task every day to fetch data files with a predefined format and creation date from the corporate storage, then copies them to an S3 bucket partitioned by date.

Processing and embeddings. EventBridge Scheduler starts a Step Functions workflow in two steps: a SageMaker BatchTransform job extracts the information from the documents and saves it to S3, then an ECS task generates the embeddings and stores them

Web frontend delivery and security. A static website is hosted on S3 behind a CloudFront distribution, with its DNS name registered in Route 53. AWS WAF inspects every request as an additional layer of security.
User routing and authentication. API Gateway authenticates users and routes requests to a Lambda function. Authentication is handled by a Cognito user pool, with the help of a Lambda@Edge function.

Orchestration and session log. The orchestrator Lambda is ultimately responsible for returning the response to the client. It first records the session in DynamoDB, then invokes the Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Lambda.

RAG query and agent inference. The RAG Lambda reads the API token from SSM Parameter Store, retrieves the relevant embeddings from Aurora and sends them with the user's query to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, which runs the agent and the LLM. The answer
